note: Synthetic, invented business assumptions for the Cost of a Silent Night model. Not real figures, forecasts or food-safety guidance. See docs/synthetic-data.md.

chain.name: Zava
chain.story: Zava runs about 400 grocery stores. The five stores on this monitor are the pilot region for the Cold Chain Monitor, the store assistant and the vendor's remote service. The board is deciding whether to roll all three out to every store.

assumptions.label: Stores in the chain
assumptions.explain: The pilot region has 5 stores. Every pilot-region cost is scaled by chain stores / 5.

assumptions.label: Nights like this per year
assumptions.explain: How often a night like tonight happens across the chain in a year. One fleet command reaches every store at once.

assumptions.label: Hold for testing after
assumptions.explain: Stock in a case above its limit for this long is held for testing. Invented for training, not food-safety guidance.

assumptions.label: Write off after
assumptions.explain: Stock above its limit for this long is written off. Invented for training, not food-safety guidance.

assumptions.label: Cost of holding stock for testing
assumptions.explain: Testing, handling and markdowns for stock that is held, as a share of its shelf value.

assumptions.label: Lost sales while shelves are empty
assumptions.explain: Shoppers who find an empty shelf buy elsewhere until the case is restocked.

assumptions.label: Night cover callout per alarm
assumptions.explain: Travel and time for night cover to handle one alarm on site.

assumptions.label: Store found warm at opening
assumptions.explain: Delayed opening, emergency stock check, deep clean and an urgent vendor visit when staff find warm cases before any alarm.

assumptions.label: False page
assumptions.explain: A page for a planned defrost that is running as scheduled. It costs a callout and teaches people to ignore alarms.

assumptions.label: Blocked planned maintenance
assumptions.explain: A planned, legitimate command that a guardrail refused or held: the vendor has to come back.

assumptions.label: Cost of a product recall and press coverage
assumptions.explain: Recall, regulator follow-up, refunds and brand damage if unsafe stock reaches shoppers.

assumptions.label: Recall chance per unnoticed warm case
assumptions.explain: A case that was held above its limit with no alarm: some of its stock may be sold before anyone notices.

assumptions.label: Recall chance when the assistant says a warm case is fine
assumptions.explain: Staff trust the store assistant. A reassuring answer about a warm case makes it far more likely the stock stays on sale.
